content.value_statement: Teams often lose task status, test discipline, and commit traceability during implementation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through TDD tasks, verification gates, and checkpoint commits.
actual_capabilities: Selects the next pending plan task and marks it in progress.
Guides red, green, and refactor work with tests first.
Runs coverage, linting, type checks, and full test suites at checkpoints.
Creates focused git commits, git notes, and SHA references.
Documents deviations, blockers, and checkpoint approvals in plan files.
limitations: It does not provide a test framework or execute checks without tool access.
It assumes the project uses Conductor track files such as plan.md.
It depends on user approval before moving past phase checkpoints.
It cannot guarantee coverage targets if the project lacks measurable tests.

use_cases.title: Implement Plan Tasks
use_cases.description: Follow a repeatable TDD cycle while moving through tasks in a Conductor plan.

use_cases.title: Verify Phase Readiness
use_cases.description: Check tests, coverage, manual verification items, and approval status before advancing a phase.

use_cases.title: Recover From Failed Checks
use_cases.description: Document failures, return to a known green state, and create remediation tasks for rejected checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Start Next Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use workflow-patterns to find the next pending task in plan.md, mark it in progress, and begin with failing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use workflow-patterns for this task. Write failing tests, implement the minimum fix, refactor safely, and report the verification commands you ran.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Phase Checkpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use workflow-patterns to verify all phase tasks, run coverage and quality gates, create manual verification steps, and wait for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Deviation or Rejection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use workflow-patterns to document this deviation, update the plan and spec if needed, create remediation tasks, and retry checkpoint approval.

output_examples.input: I need to start the next task in my Conductor plan.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the next unchecked task, marks it in progress, commits that status change, and starts with failing tests.

output_examples.input: Phase 1 looks complete. Prepare it for review.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs automated checks, summarizes coverage, creates manual verification steps, and waits for explicit approval before checkpointing.

output_examples.input: The checkpoint was rejected because validation failed.
output_examples.output: The assistant records the rejection reason, creates remediation work, fixes the failure, and repeats verification before asking for approval again.

best_practices: Keep each task in a clean TDD cycle before starting another task.
Commit status changes, implementation work, and plan updates as separate logical changes.
Request explicit user approval before creating or advancing checkpoint commits.
anti_patterns: Skipping failing tests and implementing directly.
Combining unrelated task work in a single commit.
Marking a phase complete before coverage and manual checks are reviewed.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflow guidance. The agent still follows tool permissions and should report commands before important git operations.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits projects using Conductor track plans, TDD, git commits, and phase checkpoints.

faq.question: Can I use it without Conductor?
faq.answer: Yes, but you may need to map its plan, spec, and checkpoint steps to your own files.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It improves implementation discipline, but human review is still needed for design, security, and product judgment.

faq.question: How does it handle failed tests?
faq.answer: It tells the agent to stop, diagnose the failure, and return to the last known green state.

faq.question: Why does it require approval at checkpoints?
faq.answer: Approval prevents the agent from advancing phases before automated and manual verification are complete.
